html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. JSON: JavaScript Object Notation; API: application programming interface

  • Why tool use with a JSON schema is the most reliable way to get structured output
  • The tool_choice modes for extraction
  • Schema design: required versus optional, nullable, enums with "other" and "unclear"
  • Validation and retry with error feedback, and when retry cannot help
  • Syntax errors versus semantic errors, and self-check fields

2Structured Output with Tool Use (Task 4.3)

Running case

Birchwood Supply Reads Supplier Invoices

  • Suppliers send invoices as PDFs, emails and scans
  • The system must produce clean JSON: supplier, invoice date, line items, total
  • Sometimes the text answer has broken JSON, and sometimes a required field is invented because the document does not contain it
  • Tool use with a JSON schema is the most reliable approach for schema-compliant output: define an extraction tool whose input schema is your target structure, make Claude call it, and read the data from the tool_use block's input. That removes JSON syntax errors.
  • The three tool_choice modes matter here:
tool_choice Result Use for extraction when
"auto" The model may return text instead of calling the tool Not enough if you need guaranteed structure
"any" The model must call a tool, but chooses which Several extraction schemas exist (invoice, receipt, contract) and the document type is unknown
Forced {"type":"tool","name":"extract_metadata"} The model must call that tool A particular extraction must run first, before enrichment steps

[Verify live] In current API documentation, any and forced tool are rejected (400 error) on some newer models and with manual extended thinking. The documented alternatives are strict: true on the tool (inputs guaranteed to match the schema) with auto, or structured outputs (output_config.format with a JSON schema). The exam guide teaches tool use with "any" and forced selection; answer as the guide does. As of 8 November 2026.

What a schema does not guarantee

Syntax errors (broken JSON, wrong types, missing required keys) Semantic errors (valid JSON, wrong meaning)
Examples Unclosed brace, string instead of number Line items do not sum to the total; a value placed in the wrong field
Tool use / strict schema Eliminated Not prevented
Handle with The schema itself Validation code and self-check fields

Schema design rules

  • Make a field optional or nullable when the document may not contain it. If a field is required, the model may fabricate a value to satisfy the schema.
  • Use enums for categories, with an "other" value plus a detail string so new categories do not break the schema.
  • Add an "unclear" value for genuinely ambiguous cases.
  • Put format normalization rules in the prompt (dates as YYYY-MM-DD, currency as numbers) alongside the strict schema, to handle inconsistent source formatting.
{
  "name": "extract_invoice",
  "description": "Extract fields from ONE supplier invoice. Use null for anything not in the document.",
  "input_schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "supplier": {"type": "string"},
      "invoice_date": {"type": ["string", "null"], "description": "YYYY-MM-DD"},
      "category": {"type": "string", "enum": ["goods", "freight", "services", "other", "unclear"]},
      "category_other": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
      "stated_total": {"type": ["number", "null"]},
      "calculated_total": {"type": ["number", "null"]}
    },
    "required": ["supplier", "category"]
  }
}
Exam tip

A field that may be missing must be nullable: a required field invites fabricated values.

Exam tip

Guaranteed structure with an unknown document type means tool use with tool_choice: "any" and one schema per type.

3Validation, Retry and Feedback Loops (Task 4.4)

Concept Detail
Retry with error feedback Send a follow-up request with the original document, the failed extraction and the specific validation errors, so the model can correct itself
When retry works Format mismatches, structural output errors, wrong field placement
When retry does not work The information is absent from the source (for example it lives in an external document that was not provided): another try only invites invention
Semantic validation Check sums, ranges, cross-field rules; with Pydantic or JSON Schema plus business rules
Self-correction fields Extract calculated_total next to stated_total to flag discrepancies; add a conflict_detected boolean when the source data is inconsistent
Feedback loop on findings Add a detected_pattern field (which construct triggered the finding) so you can analyze which patterns developers dismiss and fix false positives systematically
Exam tip

Validation failed because "the invoice does not list the shipping address anywhere"? → do not retry; accept null and route to review. Validation failed because "dates are in the wrong format"? → retry with the error message.

4Exam Q&A

S1A pipeline asks Claude for JSON in plain text and sometimes receives malformed output. What is the most reliable fix?

  • ARetry until the JSON parses
  • BStrip the extra text around the JSON with regular expressions and parse the rest
  • CDefine an extraction tool with a JSON schema and read the tool_use input
  • DAsk politely for valid JSON
Show the answer

Answer: C. Tool use with a schema eliminates JSON syntax errors.

S2The pipeline receives invoices, receipts and contracts, each with its own extraction tool, and the type is unknown beforehand. Claude sometimes answers in prose. Which setting is right?

  • Atool_choice: "any"
  • BNo tools
  • CForced selection of the invoice tool
  • Dtool_choice: "auto"
Show the answer

Answer: A. "any" guarantees a tool call while letting Claude choose the schema that matches the document.

S3A required purchase_order field is filled with plausible but made-up numbers for invoices that have none. What is the best schema change?

  • AShorten the field name so that the model is less tempted to fill it
  • BRemove validation
  • CAdd a second required field that holds the same purchase order number
  • DMake the field optional or nullable
Show the answer

Answer: D. A required field pushes the model to fabricate a value; a nullable field lets it say "not present".

S4The category enum has four values, but suppliers sometimes bring new kinds of charges. How should the schema evolve?

  • AMake it free text
  • BAdd an "other" value with a detail string
  • CRemove the enum and let the model answer every category as plain text
  • DReject any invoice whose category is not in the existing list of four values
Show the answer

Answer: B. "other" plus a detail string keeps structure while allowing new categories.

S5Tool use with a strict schema produces valid JSON, yet line items do not add up to the stated total on some invoices. What does this show?

  • ASchemas remove syntax errors but not semantic errors, so add validation code
  • BThe model must be retrained
  • CThe schema must be made looser
  • DStrict schemas also check arithmetic across fields, so the totals must already be right
Show the answer

Answer: A. Semantic errors need extra validation, for example comparing a calculated total with the stated one.

S6A date field fails validation because the model returned "7 Jan 2026" and the schema expects YYYY-MM-DD. What is the best retry?

  • AAsk a human immediately
  • BSkip validation
  • CSend a follow-up with the original document, the failed extraction and the specific validation error
  • DResend the exact same request unchanged, because the model will probably return a different format
Show the answer

Answer: C. Format errors are fixable when the model is shown exactly what failed.

S7Validation fails because a purchase order number is simply not in the document the pipeline has; it lives in a separate email. What should the pipeline do?

  • AAccept a null value and route the document to human review or retrieval
  • BRetry five times with stricter wording and a lower temperature on each attempt
  • CLet the model guess
  • DAdd the field to the prompt in capitals
Show the answer

Answer: A. Retry is ineffective when information is absent from the source.

S8A team wants to understand which code patterns produce findings that developers dismiss. What should they add to the structured output?

  • AA longer description field
  • BA timestamp only
  • CA random identifier
  • DA detected_pattern field recording which construct triggered each finding
Show the answer

Answer: D. Tracking the triggering pattern enables systematic analysis of dismissals.

S9Which TWO schema choices reduce fabricated values? Select TWO.

  • AMake fields nullable when the data may be absent
  • BAdd an unclear value for ambiguous cases
  • CForbid null values
  • DRemove all field descriptions
  • EMake every field required
Show the answer

Answer: A, B. Nullable fields and an explicit unclear value give the model an honest way to answer. Required fields and forbidding null push it to invent values.

S10Which TWO validation failures can retry-with-error-feedback realistically fix? Select TWO.

  • AAn unreadable scan with no text at all
  • BA field the document never contained
  • CA number placed in the wrong field
  • DA date returned in the wrong format
  • EA value that exists only in a document that was not provided
Show the answer

Answer: C, D. Format and structural mistakes can be corrected when the model sees the exact error. Absent information cannot be retried into existence.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Structured output Tool use + JSON schema; read the tool_use input; eliminates syntax errors
tool_choice auto may return text · any must call a tool (unknown type, several schemas) · forced = a named tool first
Not prevented Semantic errors (totals, wrong fields) → validation code
Schema design Optional/nullable if possibly absent · enum + other + detail · unclear · normalization rules in the prompt
Retry with feedback Document + failed output + specific errors
Retry limits Useless when info is absent; works for format/structure errors
Self-check calculated_total vs stated_total · conflict_detected · detected_pattern
